title: Un bel appartement : place et formes des adjectifs
summary: Place familiar short adjectives before nouns, distinguish neuf from nouveau, and use bel, nouvel and vieil correctly.
objectives: Place common adjectives before or after the noun appropriately.
Choose beau/bel/belle, nouveau/nouvel/nouvelle and vieux/vieil/vieille with their plurals.
Distinguish brand-new from newly acquired and recognise fol/mol.

sections.title: Most descriptions follow the noun; some frequent short adjectives precede it
paragraphs: Colour, nationality and many descriptive adjectives normally follow the noun: une voiture rouge, un étudiant canadien. Familiar short adjectives often come before it: petit (small), grand (big/tall), jeune (young), joli (pretty), bon (good), mauvais (bad), beau (beautiful), vieux (old), nouveau (new), premier (first), dernier (last). This is a useful list, not a universal length rule. Several adjectives can change meaning with position, such as un grand homme (a great man) versus un homme grand (a tall man).

When an adjective comes before a plural noun, careful French usually uses de rather than indefinite des: de petits sacs. Fixed combinations and conversational variants exist; the exercises specify the ordinary careful construction. For pointing to a noun, use ce (masculine), cet (masculine before a vowel or silent h), cette (feminine), ces (plural). These mean this/that or these/those and replace the article.
points: Un appartement (m.) = an apartment; une voiture (f.) = a car.

examples.note: Petite precedes the noun; the colour follows it.
The ordinary careful indefinite plural is de before a pre-noun adjective.
Cet is masculine before a vowel; it is not feminine cette.

mistakes.why: A simple identifying colour normally follows the noun in this neutral description.

sections.title: A following vowel changes the masculine singular, not the noun's gender
paragraphs: Immediately before a masculine singular noun beginning with a vowel or silent h, use bel, nouvel and vieil instead of beau, nouveau and vieux. Before a consonant use the ordinary masculine form. After the noun or after être use beau, nouveau or vieux again. Feminines are belle, nouvelle, vieille. Masculine plurals are beaux, nouveaux, vieux; feminine plurals are belles, nouvelles, vieilles.

Fou (mad/crazy) and mou (soft) have feminine folle and molle, masculine plurals fous and mous, feminine plurals folles and molles. Their pre-vowel masculine forms fol and mol are mostly literary or fixed-use recognition forms. Ordinary speech usually chooses the adjective after the noun: un espoir fou, un oreiller mou. Do not force fol or mol into every everyday description.
points: An aspirated h blocks the pre-vowel form: un vieux héros.

examples.french: un **bel** appartement / un appartement **beau** et lumineux
examples.english: a beautiful apartment / an apartment that is beautiful and bright
examples.note: Bel immediately precedes the vowel; beau is used after the noun.

examples.english: a new hotel / a new house
examples.note: Silent h triggers nouvel; feminine uses nouvelle.

examples.french: un **vieil** ami / de **vieux** amis / de **vieilles** amies
examples.english: an old friend / old friends / old female friends
examples.note: The special masculine singular is not the plural form.
Masculine plural adds x; feminine plural adds s.
Nouveau has the same -x/-s plural contrast.

examples.french: Dans le poème, il garde un **fol** espoir.
examples.english: In the poem, he keeps a wild hope.
examples.note: Literary recognition: fol before masculine vowel-initial espoir.

examples.english: The text describes a soft pillow.
examples.note: Literary recognition; everyday un oreiller mou is more usual.

mistakes.why: Appartement is masculine; bel, not feminine belle, precedes the vowel.
After être use beau, not the pre-noun form bel.

sections.title: New to someone is not necessarily brand-new
paragraphs: Nouveau usually comes before the noun and means new in the situation, recently obtained, different or additional. Neuf normally follows the noun and means newly made or unused. A newly purchased second-hand bicycle can be mon nouveau vélo without being neuf. Neuf changes to neuve, neufs, neuves.
points: Choose the intended meaning before choosing the adjective.

examples.note: It is new to me, not newly manufactured.
Neuf indicates unused condition and agrees with feminine plural chaussures.

sections.title: Count, rank and newness answer different questions
paragraphs: A count tells how many; a rank selects which ones in an ordered group. The count comes before the rank in les trois premières pages: three pages, specifically the first three. Both precede the noun, and premières agrees with pages. An adjective can also precede a personal proper name in a descriptive phrase such as la jeune Salomé, especially in narration.

Nouveau is the ordinary choice for someone newly joining a situation: une nouvelle collègue. Neuf describes unused or newly made things, so it is not the normal adjective for a new colleague or a newly adopted animal. The person or animal need not be newly born to be nouveau in your life.

examples.french: Lisez **les trois premières pages**, pas seulement la troisième.
examples.english: Read the first three pages, not only the third.
examples.note: Trois counts the pages; premières selects the beginning of the sequence.

examples.english: We are keeping the last two seats.
examples.note: The count precedes the agreeing ordinal adjective.

examples.french: Dans la pièce, **la jeune Salomé** entre en scène.
examples.english: In the play, young Salomé comes onstage.
examples.note: The descriptive adjective can come before a personal name.

examples.english: Our new colleague has a lot of experience.
examples.note: New to the team does not mean inexperienced or unused.

practice.prompt: Order these words to mean the first two rows: 'premières / les / rangées / deux'.
practice.explanation: The count deux comes before the rank premières, which agrees with rangées.

practice.prompt: Does 'les quatre derniers chapitres' mean four chapters at the end, or only chapter four?
practice.explanation: Quatre counts the chapters; derniers locates them at the end of the sequence.

practice.prompt: Keep the descriptive adjective before the personal name. Order: 'jeune / le / Malik'.
practice.explanation: A descriptive adjective may precede a personal proper name in this kind of phrase.

practice.prompt: Choose nouvelle or neuve for a person joining a team: 'C'est notre ___ collègue.'
practice.explanation: A colleague is new to the situation, not an unused manufactured object.

practice.prompt: Can 'notre nouveau chat' describe an adult cat adopted yesterday?
practice.explanation: Nouveau can mean new to the household, regardless of the animal's age.

practice.prompt: Select nouveau or neuf for the newly appointed director: 'Le ___ directeur travaille déjà ici depuis dix ans.'
practice.explanation: The director is new in that role even if not new to the organisation.

practice.prompt: Supply beau before masculine hôtel: 'un ___ hôtel'.
practice.explanation: Silent h triggers bel.

practice.prompt: Supply vieux before feminine maison: 'une ___ maison'.
practice.explanation: The feminine form is vieille.

practice.prompt: The bicycle is new to you but second-hand. Which phrase communicates this without claiming it is unused?
practice.explanation: Nouveau can mean newly acquired.

practice.prompt: Arrange these words in the neutral order: une / voiture / rouge / petite.
practice.explanation: Petite precedes the noun; rouge follows.

practice.prompt: Supply nouveau: 'un ___ emploi' (emploi is masculine).
practice.explanation: Use nouvel before a masculine singular vowel.

practice.prompt: Supply beau: 'de ___ arbres'.
practice.explanation: The masculine plural is beaux even before a vowel.

practice.prompt: Supply nouveau: 'de ___ écoles'.
practice.explanation: Écoles is feminine plural.

practice.prompt: Supply vieux: 'un ___ immeuble'.
practice.explanation: The masculine singular vowel triggers vieil.

practice.prompt: Use neuf with feminine plural bottes: 'des bottes ___'.
practice.explanation: Neuf becomes neuve, then neuves.

practice.prompt: In careful French, supply de or des: '___ petits jardins'.
practice.explanation: An ordinary adjective before a plural noun generally changes indefinite des to de.

practice.prompt: A poem uses 'un fol espoir'. Which modern adjective does fol represent?
practice.explanation: Fol is the literary pre-vowel masculine form of fou.

practice.prompt: In 'un mol oreiller', which everyday post-noun form corresponds to mol?
practice.explanation: Mol is masculine singular before a vowel; mou is the usual post-noun form.

practice.prompt: Supply beau: 'Cette place est ___.'
practice.explanation: A feminine place requires belle.

practice.prompt: Supply vieux: 'de ___ livres'.
practice.explanation: Masculine vieux is unchanged in the plural.

practice.prompt: Supply ce, cet or cette: '___ hôtel'.
practice.explanation: Hôtel is masculine and begins with silent h.

practice.prompt: Supply mou: 'des couvertures ___'.
practice.explanation: Mou has feminine molle, then plural molles.

production_task.prompt: Describe a newly acquired second-hand object and a place you like. Include nouveau, a beau-family form and a colour in its neutral position.
production_task.model_answer: J'ai un nouveau vélo d'occasion. Il est rouge. Près de chez moi, il y a un bel hôtel.
production_task.translation: I have a new second-hand bicycle. It is red. Near my home, there is a beautiful hotel.
rubric: Use nouveau without implying unused condition.
Use bel before a masculine noun with silent h.
Use ordinary adjective agreement and position.
